summary: Probed XSS vectors across multiple injection points in the OWASP Juice Shop application at http://127.0.0.1:3010. Confirmed reflected XSS via search q parameter (Angular SPA uses bypassSecurityTrustHtml on the search term and renders via innerHTML). Confirmed stored XSS via product reviews API (PUT /rest/products/1/reviews stores unsanitized HTML/script payloads). Feedback form has server-side sanitization that strips dangerous tags but allows basic HTML; feedback comments are rendered via bypassSecurityTrustHtml in the SPA. The DOM XSS challenge (localXssChallenge) is already solved, confirming the search q parameter XSS. Product descriptions also use bypassSecurityTrustHtml for rendering. Basket/comments and user profile fields could not be tested without valid authenticated session.

candidates.title: Reflected XSS via search q parameter (DOM XSS)
candidates.claim: Reflected XSS allows arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser via the search query parameter. Angular's DomSanitizer is bypassed using bypassSecurityTrustHtml and the value is rendered via innerHTML.
candidates.poc_hint: Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3010/#/search?q=<iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)"></iframe>. The iframe payload is set as searchValue via bypassSecurityTrustHtml and rendered via innerHTML in the search results heading. The DOM XSS challenge (localXssChallenge id=20) is already solved, confirming this vulnerability.

candidates.title: Stored XSS via Product Reviews API
candidates.claim: The product reviews API accepts unsanitized HTML/script payloads, enabling stored XSS. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes when users view the product page.
candidates.poc_hint: Send PUT request to /rest/products/1/reviews with JSON body {"message":"<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>","author":"test@test.com"}. The payload is stored as-is and returned in GET /rest/products/1/reviews. Product descriptions are also rendered via bypassSecurityTrustHtml.

candidates.title: Stored XSS via Feedback Comments (with server-side filter bypass)
candidates.claim: Feedback comments are rendered via bypassSecurityTrustHtml. Although server-side sanitization strips script/img/iframe tags, basic HTML like <b> passes through, and a filter bypass could enable XSS.
candidates.poc_hint: POST to /api/Feedbacks with {"comment":"bold test","rating":3,"captchaId":1,"captcha":"6"}. The tag is stored and rendered. The bypassSecurityTrustHtml call confirms the XSS surface if a filter bypass is found.

facts.summary: XSS probe results - Confirmed reflected XSS in search, stored XSS in product reviews, feedback comments use bypassSecurityTrustHtml
Found XSS vectors: 1. Reflected XSS via search q parameter 2. Stored XSS via product reviews 3. Stored XSS in feedback 4. Product descriptions use bypassSecurityTrustHtml

deadends: Basket/comments endpoint requires valid JWT authentication - could not test without valid session (JWT token from registration was rejected for PUT requests)
User profile fields (username, email) - PUT /api/Users/:id requires valid JWT authentication which was rejected
Feedback form server-side filter strips dangerous tags (
Reflected XSS challenge (reflectedXssChallenge) and API-only XSS (restfulXssChallenge) are disabled on Docker
CSP Bypass, Client-side XSS Protection, HTTP-Header XSS, Video XSS challenges are all disabled on Docker
